moves.name: Pad per-expert token runs to BLOCK_M for routed GEMM tiles
moves.description: moe_align_block_size groups flattened (token, top-k slot) pairs by expert, pads each expert run to a BLOCK_M multiple, and emits sorted_token_ids/expert_ids/num_tokens_post_pad for the Triton fused_moe kernel.
moves.problem_solved: Avoids mixed-expert tiles and enables contiguous per-expert GEMM blocks.

occurrences.acknowledges_prior: yes: SGLang header cites vLLM fused_moe.py

occurrences.evidence: every bucket is padded to a block_size multiple

semantic_preconditions: topk_ids are flattened token-slot expert ids
pad slots use numel and are masked by fused_moe
expert_ids index one expert per BLOCK_M tile
hardware_preconditions: CUDA/HIP capable GPU for kernel paths
framework_preconditions: topk_ids and output buffers are contiguous

assumptions.assumption: Each padded tile belongs to one expert.
assumptions.excerpt: sorted_token_ids by expert index and padding ensures divisibility

assumptions.assumption: Pad slots are masked before loading token data.

moves.performance_evidence: None isolated at first import; #32395 explains launch-bound costs.

biography.first_appearance: vLLM #2453, commit 5d60def02c (2024-01-29), added csrc/moe_align_block_size_kernels.cu for DeepSeekMoE; SGLang #484 (09de730dee, 2024-05-27) brought the same padded per-expert sorted-token contract into its Triton fused_moe path.
biography.problem: Converts flattened token/top-k expert ids into contiguous expert runs padded to BLOCK_M, so routed GEMM tiles never mix experts and can read expert_ids/num_tokens_post_pad cheaply.
biography.preconditions: topk_ids are valid flattened expert ids; padding sentinel rows are masked by consumers; each BLOCK_M tile is assigned one expert; output buffers are contiguous and sized for post-pad count.
biography.survival: textual + evidence: git grep at 89e1316e finds moe_align_block_size, CEILDIV(...block_size), padded_count/sorted ids; release samples show presence from v0.1.17/v0.4.x through v0.5.20.
biography.recurrence: SGLang reimplemented/optimized it in sgl-kernel (#2579/#3347); vLLM #12574 explicitly ported SGLang ded9fcd/ba5112ff back, and vLLM #19572 later optimized the CUDA kernel with padded_num_experts/experts_per_warp.
biography.failures: No direct failure in failure-links; related align optimizations were reverted under the two-phase/multi-block move, not the padding contract itself.
biography.acknowledgement: vLLM #12574 commit body says "sgl_moe_align_block_size is based on" SGLang ded9fcd and "moe_align_block_size is based on" SGLang ba5112ff.

moves.name: Shared-memory cumsum plus separate multi-block token sort
moves.description: The align kernel computes per-expert counts and padded cumulative offsets in shared memory, then a separate sort/count kernel scatters tokens with atomics into those ranges. Later code adds warp-level shared-memory scans.
moves.problem_solved: Lets many CTAs sort tokens while preserving padded expert ranges.

atomicAdd order within an expert is not semantically observed
hardware_preconditions: shared memory holds counts, prefixes, scan buffer and warp sums
framework_preconditions: generic path launches align before count_and_sort on the same stream

assumptions.assumption: Intra-expert scatter order is irrelevant to consumers.
assumptions.excerpt: Every pair writes its own output row

assumptions.assumption: Warp scan path assumes WARP_SIZE lanes.

moves.performance_evidence: #3613 reports 3x-6x speedup but was reverted; #19572 optimizes the vLLM port.

biography.first_appearance: SGLang #3347, commit cdae77b03d (2025-02-07), added sgl-kernel moe_align_kernel.cu with moe_token_sort_kernel, cumsum_buffer, and atomicAdd scatter.
biography.problem: Lets alignment scale beyond a single serial expert-count pass by separating padded cumsum construction from token sorting/scatter while preserving expert-padded ranges.
biography.preconditions: cumsum_buffer must be initialized to padded offsets before scatter; atomicAdd order within an expert must be semantically unobserved; kernels run on one stream; warp/block scan code assumes CUDA-style WARP_SIZE.
biography.survival: textual + evidence: cutoff 89e1316e contains count_and_sort_expert_tokens_kernel and warp_exclusive_scan(padded_count); release samples find it in v0.4.4/v0.4.5 and v0.5.2-v0.5.20.
biography.recurrence: #3613 tried a multi-block follow-up; #3982 reverted it pending modification; later #19572 in vLLM ported the SGLang cdae77 lineage and rewrote around padded_num_experts/experts_per_warp.
biography.failures: confirmed-reverts.csv sglang:18bb216c records the #3613 multi-block optimization revert; later SGLang events remove/reintroduce block/warp scan variants.
biography.acknowledgement: vLLM #19572 subject names optimizing moe_align_block_size; #12574 already acknowledged SGLang sources. SGLang #3613 PR text called it a follow-up of moe-align-with-multiple-blocks-execution.

moves.problem_solved: Replaces Python/Torch routing pipelines and intermediate tensors with one routing kernel.

Kimi K2 variant supports NUM_EXPERTS in {256,384}
framework_preconditions: input and bias are 2D/1D fp32 for generic JIT wrapper
shared experts use appended expert ids >= num_experts

biography.first_appearance: vLLM #2769, commit f0d4e14557 (2024-02-05), added a fused top-k softmax MoE kernel adapted from TensorRT-LLM; SGLang #4302 cherry-picked the vLLM template.

moves.name: Fuse routed_scaling_factor into gate output or MoE combine reduction
moves.description: SGLang folds routed_scaling_factor into either routing gate weights or the fused top-k combine/reduce kernel instead of a separate multiply. Current code passes the factor into moe_sum_reduce and can apply it in moe_fused_gate output when requested.
moves.problem_solved: Eliminates standalone scale multiplies and reduces combine-path memory traffic.

gate-output scaling must preserve renormalization semantics

topk==1 and factor==1 may bypass combine

Gate-output scaling is optional and explicit.

biography.first_appearance: SGLang #6220, commit 515ef4facb (2025-06-07), fused routed_scaling_factor into topk_reduce; later SGLang #8770/#10321 moved the same idea into gate output or CUDA sum-reduce.

biography.recurrence: The first topk_reduce version was reverted (#6968), relanded/reworked, moved into moe_fused_gate (#8770), reverted again (#9035), and reappeared in moe_sum_reduce (#10321). Current vLLM/TRT-LLM MoE paths also carry routed_scaling_factor plumbing.

output buffer is preallocated and contiguous
